title: Liber III opens — dove-eyes needed to see the Word
english: The Third Book. The greatness in the Word cannot first be seen or known unless one first receives dove-eyes — that is, spiritual understanding. The couch she says she shares with the Bridegroom seems to me to indicate this body of the soul, in which, while still placed there, she has been counted worthy to be taken into the Word’s companionship.
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: Shaded couch; believers without contemplation
english: And she recalls it as shaded — not dry, but fruitful and as if wooded with the density of good work. But the Bride says these things — at least the soul that already has dove-eyes. Those who only believe the Bridegroom, yet could not perceive how great is the beauty in God’s Word, say: [[We saw him, and he had no form >> Bible:Isaiah 53:2]].
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: Cedar beams and cypress paneling of the house
english: [[The beams of our houses are cedar, our paneling cypress >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:17]]. God’s house is the church; the beams apostles and prophets; the paneling the orders of the saints. Cedar is incorruptible: uncorrupted teaching. Cypress has fragrance and height: a life that is fragrant and tends toward heaven.
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: I am the flower of the field and lily of the valleys
english: [[I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:1]]. Christ calls himself the flower of the field, who appeared in the world for all; the lily of the valleys, because he offers himself to the lowly. [[As a lily among thorns, so is my friend among the daughters >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:2]]: the church bright among piercing tribulations.
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: As an apple tree among trees of the wood
english: [[As an apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. Under his shadow whom I desired I sat, and his fruit was sweet to my throat >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:3]]. The apple tree is Christ; the trees of the wood are other humans. His shadow is protection; his fruit teaching and immortality.
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: He brought me to the wine cellar; order love
english: [[He brought me into the wine cellar; he ordered love in me >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:4]]. The wine cellar is the mysteries of the passion and of the eucharist. He ordered love: not chaotic, but ordered — first God, then neighbor. [[Stay me with flowers, heap me with apples, for I languish with love >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:5]].
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: Left hand under my head; I adjure you
english: [[His left hand under my head, and his right hand will embrace me >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:6]]. The left is dispensation of temporal things; the right gift of eternal things. [[I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and stags of the field, not to raise or awaken the beloved until she please >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:7]].
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: The voice of my beloved leaping on the mountains
english: [[The voice of my beloved; behold, he comes leaping on the mountains, springing over the hills. My beloved is like a gazelle and a young stag. Behold, he stands behind our wall, looking through the windows, peering through the lattices >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:8-9]]. The Word’s coming is swift and subtle.
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: Arise; winter is past; the turtledove’s voice
english: [[My beloved speaks to me: Arise, make haste, my friend, my dove, my fair one, and come. For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone. The flowers have appeared in the land; the time of pruning has come; the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:10-12]].
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: Fig and vines; dove in the clefts of the rock
english: [[The fig tree has put forth its green figs; the flowering vines have given fragrance. Arise, my friend, my fair one, and come. My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hollow of the wall. Show me your face; let your voice sound in my ears >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:13-14]]. This is the Third Book’s first series, from the shaded couch as far as the turtledove’s voice and the cleft of the rock.
translator_notes: Liber III after Liber II CLOSEOUT.

title: Show me your face; beside the outer wall
english: [[Show me your face; let your voice sound in my ears, for your voice is sweet and your face is fair >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:14]]. The Bridegroom, who had come leaping on the mountains and looking through the windows, says a second time: Arise, come; now he adds the place: in the covert of the rock beside the outer wall. The outer wall is a wall before the wall — a more secret place where, the veil removed, the face may be shown and the voice heard.

title: Winter of the soul; spring and going out
english: The historical telling of winter and spring is of little consequence; everything must be carried over to spiritual understanding. The soul’s winter is the waves of passions and the storms of vices. In winter God’s Word does not urge going outdoors, but fortifying within the walls. The soul’s spring is quiet and calm; then the Word calls her to go out beyond flesh and world.

title: Catch us the little foxes — soul reading
english: [[Catch us the little foxes that spoil the vineyards; and our vineyards will flower >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:15]]. The person changes: the Bridegroom speaks to his companions. Foxes in the soul are contrary powers and crooked thoughts destroying the flower of the virtues. Holy angels are to catch them while they are little, before consent and the deed of sin.

title: Foxes as heretics; little vines and the perfect
english: Of Christ and the church: the foxes are perverse teachers of heresies, who by clever arguments spoil the Lord’s vineyard. Teachers of the church receive power to catch foxes, as to tread on serpents. Little vineyards — unformed souls — can be hurt; the perfect are not easily scandalized. Catch for us: for me the Bridegroom and for the Bride, or for me and my companions.

title: Liber III historical recapitulation
english: Historical recapitulation of Book III: from the shaded couch and dove-eyes through cedar beams and the flower of the field, the apple among the trees, the wine cellar, left hand and right, the leaping voice, winter past, the fig and the hollow of the rock, as far as the showing of the face and the catching of the foxes.

title: Liber III spiritual recapitulation
english: Spiritual recapitulation: dove-eyes are spiritual understanding; the couch a fruitful body; cedar and cypress incorruptible teaching and life; flower and lily Christ for the lowly; the apple the Word’s sweetness; the cellar the mysteries; ordered charity; winter of vices and spring of virtues; the rock the Word’s secret; foxes little thoughts and heresies to be caught.

title: Daughters of Jerusalem and going out
english: In Book III the daughters of Jerusalem receive teaching about the soul’s going out: not to go outdoors in the winter of passions, but after calm to obey the Word. Those without dove-eyes think the drama’s letter empty; those who have them recognize winter and spring, rock and foxes in the soul.

title: Order of love closing Liber III
english: The order of love in Book III: from sharing the couch to praise of the flowers, from the apple’s shadow to the cellar of charity, from guarded sleep to the leaping voice, from winter enclosures to showing the face in the rock, from the vineyard’s flower to catching the foxes. Here the steps of the one who progresses are closed.

title: Caveat — Liber III/IV MSS and spiritual reading
english: Caveat: Baehrens notes that most manuscripts do not separate the Fourth Book from the Third; the edition inserts [LIBER QUARTUS] at Arise, come. Let us warn the reader that the nuptial words are to be understood spiritually of the Word and the soul, or of Christ and the church, lest the letter cause scandal.

title: Liber III CLOSEOUT — toward Liber Quartus
english: End of the Third Book (our series 20/20). The Fourth Book follows editorially from Arise, come and winter past, where Rufinus expounds more fully, as far as Catch the foxes and Amen at the end of the surviving commentary. Thus far, from the shaded couch through the hollow of the rock and the little foxes, with the Lord’s help, we have set in order. Amen.
